stories.headline: Generated dungeons gain a live inspection view with five optional map overlays
stories.summary: CUSTODIAN's procedural arena now has a runtime inspector showing detached snapshots and five optional, bounded overlays for terrain, routes, playability, sites and vistas. The implementation merged to main after focused validation. Main-branch Godot and repository checks are still running; interactive gameplay remains unverified.
stories.body: The procgen gallery can now inspect the accepted generated arena through its runtime map APIs, rather than treating generation as an opaque operation. Five optional overlays expose terrain, route, playability, sites and vistas, with a 1,024-descriptor limit per layer and overlays off by default. Snapshot refresh responds to arena replacement and cancellation, and teardown invalidates stale data. Focused validation reported 8/8 passing checks, while an earlier Godot pipeline had unrelated authored-level failures. The merge to main is verified, but its new main checks were still in progress at observation and no interactive gameplay proof was observed.
bullets: Inspect the accepted generated arena with five opt-in map overlays
Overlay data is capped and disabled by default
Focused validation reported 8/8 passed before merge
Next: main CI results and an interactive inspector demonstration

article.lead: CUSTODIAN's procedural dungeon can now explain what it generated. A new inspection panel and five optional map overlays reveal the arena's terrain, routes, playable regions, sites and vistas, giving designers a clearer view of the world beneath the scene.

sections.heading: A window into generated geography
sections.text: The inspector reads a detached snapshot of the accepted arena using the existing runtime map APIs. Its overlays are optional and individually bounded, so inspection need not flood the gallery with visual markers.

sections.heading: Inspection follows the world, not stale results
sections.text: The implementation refreshes when the accepted arena changes and invalidates snapshots on cancellation or teardown. That matters when testers repeatedly regenerate the same dungeon or explore new seeds.

sections.heading: The remaining proof boundary
sections.text: The implementation landed on main and focused tests were reported passing. At observation, main-branch CI was still in progress and a hands-on interactive demonstration had not been confirmed.

insights.title: Procgen is becoming inspectable
insights.explanation: Visualizing routes and playability makes generated levels easier to debug and refine, connecting the earlier seed controls to practical design iteration.

insights.title: Bounded overlays protect usability
insights.explanation: The default-off, capped layers keep inspection optional rather than overwhelming the dungeon presentation.

article.takeaway: A runtime inspector is integrated into main, making generated dungeon structure visible to developers; final main CI and interactive validation remain open.
article.next_watch: Check main Godot pipeline and demonstrate overlay refresh after seed rerolls, cancellation and arena replacement.

stories.summary: The procgen gallery now includes a generation panel for repeating a seed, choosing a new seed, cancelling pending generation and viewing errors. The changes merged to main; automated smoke is registered, but a passing main CI or interactive playthrough has not been confirmed.
stories.body: The procedural dungeon showcase gained a generation session and visible controls. Players or testers can enter a numeric seed, regenerate the same layout or reroll; the only validated preset currently uses the 96×96 Sundered Keep Ascent arena with 12 rooms. A staged candidate is kept separate from the accepted arena, and regeneration is disabled while the Operator is inside. article.lead: CUSTODIAN's generated dungeon is no longer locked to one hard-coded run. The gallery now has a seed-and-regenerate control panel, turning its arena into something testers can explore repeatedly while keeping the existing Operator and camera intact.

sections.heading: A dungeon you can regenerate
sections.text: The new panel exposes the selected seed and generation status, with repeat-the-same-seed, reroll, cancellation and error feedback. The initial preset is deliberately narrow: Sundered Keep Ascent, 96×96 cells and 12 rooms. Other profiles and sizes are not yet proven.

sections.heading: Protect the world already on screen
sections.text: A session controller separates the accepted arena from a staging candidate, rejects stale generation results and prevents replacement while the Operator occupies the arena. This addresses a real usability problem: trying another map should not unexpectedly strand or duplicate the player.

sections.heading: What is and is not proven
sections.text: The source and registered focused Godot smoke landed in main. The smoke covers deterministic generation, cancellation, map lifecycle and Operator/camera identity, but this inspection did not establish a passing main CI run or a human interactive playthrough.

insights.title: Reproducible worlds make debugging practical
insights.explanation: Repeating a seed gives artists and gameplay developers a stable environment for comparing changes, while rerolling allows variation without manually editing the level.

insights.title: The safe replacement boundary is part of the feature
insights.explanation: Preserving the accepted arena until a new candidate is ready keeps generation experiments from disrupting the existing player route.

article.takeaway: Generation controls are integrated into main with a bounded initial preset; runtime and interactive validation remain the next proof gates.
article.next_watch: Confirm the registered Godot smoke on main and demonstrate same-seed repeat, reroll, cancellation and safe return in an interactive session.

stories.headline: CUSTODIAN retires mandatory paired reviews, removing a long-standing development gate
stories.summary: An owner-approved workflow change removes mandatory post-landing paired reviews. Implementation packets now advance on focused validation and owner review, while historical review records remain archived. This clears a procedural bottleneck, not a gameplay milestone.
stories.body: The owner retired mandatory paired post-land reviews on November 12. The merged policy and dispatcher changes make pairing advisory for implementation work, allow single-packet authoring, and redirect dependencies away from retired reviews. The migration record reports 161 implementation/correction packets switched to Review: none, 127 dependency rewrites, and 265 review packets archived intact. These are migration-record counts, not live dispatcher totals. Focused validation and owner inspection remain required. The source landing is verified; fresh full dispatcher audit, runtime claimability and resulting product progress are not verified here.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN has removed a review requirement that had delayed development. New implementation work no longer needs a matching post-landing reviewer packet, although focused tests and owner inspection still matter. This is a change to the development path, not evidence that new gameplay is already available.

sections.heading: A simpler path from implementation to integration
sections.text: The dispatcher now treats implementation pairing mismatches as advisory rather than blocking. Authoring can promote a single implementation or correction packet instead of manufacturing a paired review. Existing review records remain preserved for historical accountability.

sections.heading: What the migration actually changes
sections.text: The retirement record reports 161 implementation/correction packets changed to no paired review, 127 dependencies redirected to implementation work, and 265 review packets archived. These are recorded migration operations, not a live measurement of runnable work.

sections.heading: Why this matters for the game
sections.text: Operator, art, environment and procgen work can now move through a shorter procedural route. That reduces friction but does not itself create a playable feature, validate a host process or establish that a blocked workstream has resumed.

insights.title: The bottleneck was policy, not necessarily implementation
insights.explanation: Retiring the paired-review dependency removes a mandatory procedural step. The next meaningful proof is whether substantive product work lands with focused validation.

insights.title: Historical evidence survives the reset
insights.explanation: The review archive was retained rather than deleted, so the change does not require rewriting prior outcomes.

article.takeaway: The project has deliberately simplified its acceptance workflow; user-visible progress remains the measure of success.
article.next_watch: A verified Operator, animation, environment or gameplay landing under the revised workflow, plus a fresh dispatcher audit showing actual eligibility.

stories.body: The Crèche now has a committed Blender construction script, reference artwork, dimensions and an explicit verification plan. The design reserves gameplay circulation and attachment points for modular architectural pieces. Its authoring dimensions are choices inferred from illustrations, not measured physical geometry. The kit's README explicitly says the script has only been syntax-checked and has not been run in Blender; no generated .blend, .glb or game-level runtime proof is established. Next: run the build and verifier, inspect the resulting preview and openings, then test integration without replacing an existing level.

sections.heading: From illustration to room geometry
sections.text: The kit defines an interior floor, perimeter walls, three north window openings and a south doorway. It also keeps the central floor, side bays and exit passage clear for future gameplay. The scale and heights are deliberate design assumptions, not dimensions measured from the illustration.

sections.heading: A home for modular art
sections.text: Named sockets reserve positions for sleeping alcoves, gothic windows, columns, archways, trim and rubble. These placeholders make the next asset-fitting pass more systematic without pretending that the finished 3D meshes are already imported.

sections.heading: What is still unproven
sections.text: The README says the Blender script passed syntax checking but has not been run in Blender. The editable project, GLB export, preview, manifest verification and engine integration must still be demonstrated.

insights.explanation: The next meaningful leap is verified Blender output and a game-camera test, not another planning or review transition.

stories.headline: Feature spotlight: the Operator's shadow-casting flashlight
stories.summary: A retrospective look at CUSTODIAN's existing Operator flashlight: a directional warm beam casts shadows while a softer local glow helps nearby visibility. The Godot implementation and smoke-test source exist; this is not a new launch or an independently verified runtime demo.
stories.body: This is a retrospective spotlight on an existing Godot component, inspected November 11, 2026. The Operator carries an aim-directed flashlight that starts off and toggles using the configured input. A warm, shadow-casting PointLight2D beam and an unshadowed nearby glow serve separate visual roles. The design documents the Undergate Mechanism Hall as the first flashlight-dominant environment. Source and smoke-test scripts are present; this report has not run Godot or captured in-game proof.

article.lead: An archive spotlight, not breaking news: CUSTODIAN already has a flashlight component for its Operator. The warm, aim-directed beam casts shadows, while a second, softer glow helps reveal nearby space. The actual Godot scene, script, and test source were inspected on November 11, 2026; this feature's original release date is not established here.

sections.heading: Two jobs for one flashlight
sections.text: The scene combines a focused shadow-casting beam with a broad, unshadowed glow. This preserves meaningful darkness and geometry while keeping the Operator's immediate surroundings legible.

sections.heading: Equipment without busywork
sections.text: The flashlight is permanent equipment. It starts off, toggles on demand, and follows the Operator's existing aim vector. When the aim briefly becomes zero, the beam holds its last valid facing. The current design intentionally avoids battery, durability, loot, and upgrade systems.

sections.heading: Built for authored darkness
sections.text: Design notes name the Undergate Mechanism Hall as a flashlight-dominant environment with machinery occluders and selective light pools. That's an authored vision supported by source files, not proof of a newly played or captured build.

insights.title: Exploration becomes a lighting problem
insights.explanation: A beam that actually casts shadows invites authored machinery, occlusion, and local light to participate in how a space is explored.

insights.title: A single aim source keeps controls coherent
insights.explanation: The flashlight follows the Operator's own aim direction rather than maintaining a competing input system, and keeps its orientation through brief zero-input moments.

article.takeaway: The flashlight is implemented in source with distinct shadow and glow behavior. No fresh runtime validation or visual demonstration is claimed.
article.next_watch: A recorded Godot smoke run and a public, verified in-game image of the Undergate Mechanism Hall would establish the next level of evidence.

stories.headline: Worker isolation proof merges into main, with security acceptance still incomplete
stories.summary: PR #140 merged a disabled, manually invoked isolated-worker proof and bounded host diagnostics into main. This is a code landing, not independent security acceptance or worker activation; unresolved loopback and dependency/model proof gaps remain.
stories.body: Main 82e1a811 merges PR #140, adding a systemd worker template, launcher, provisioning and validation tools, tests, and bounded diagnostic evidence. Earlier PR evidence reported 13 focused tests passing, but also documented incomplete security acceptance, including a loopback anomaly, LFS retrieval timeout and unavailable isolated model execution. No fresh independent PASS, running worker, canonical dispatcher audit, or verified teardown was established. The private pilot pointer remains dated November 8 and is stale; no operational counts were used.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN's isolated-worker proof has moved from an open proposal into main. The merge adds a deliberately controlled execution boundary and its validation tools, but does not certify that boundary or turn on a worker.

sections.heading: A safer execution path is now in the codebase
sections.text: The merge introduces a systemd service template, worker launcher, provisioning checks, validation code and bounded diagnostic records. These components provide a concrete basis for review rather than an active unattended executor.

sections.heading: The security gate is still open
sections.text: Earlier evidence reported focused tests passing, alongside unresolved loopback behavior and incomplete dependency/model checks. Landing the implementation does not convert those gaps into an independent acceptance receipt.

insights.title: Landing makes review possible, not optional
insights.explanation: The project can now review an exact main revision of the worker boundary, but it still needs convincing evidence that isolation holds under the intended execution conditions.

insights.title: No automatic execution follows from this merge
insights.explanation: The worker design is deliberately disabled and manually invoked. No verified activation, host process or cleanup evidence accompanies this GitHub landing.

article.takeaway: The isolated-worker proof is merged but remains unaccepted for production execution.

stories.body: At main a16fb3ece74f90358dac36d1b981348efeaba412, worker-isolation PR #140 remains open, not merged. Its description reports 13 focused tests passed and systemd/security checks passed, but an unexplained loopback anomaly, timed-out anonymous LFS retrieval, and unavailable isolated model execution prevent full proof acceptance. The proposed systemd worker is explicitly disabled/inactive with no timer. Scheduled Automatic Packet Authoring Handoff run 42976298927 (November 11, 07:00 UTC) failed in 'Validate and publish explicitly authorized pairs'; the specific underlying error is not established by the inspected job step summary. A preceding scheduled run at 00:13 UTC passed. No host dispatcher audit or fresh private WIRE observation was available. The November 8 pointer is stale. These are bounded GitHub observations, not live process or workstream totals.

article.lead: A proposed isolated worker has reached pull-request review, but CUSTODIAN has not yet demonstrated the full security boundary it needs. Meanwhile, the latest scheduled packet-authoring handoff failed during validation and publication, leaving automatic handoff health uncertain.

sections.heading: The worker is built to stay off until proven safe
sections.text: PR #140 adds a manually invoked systemd proof worker, launcher-level network checks and redacted host evidence. Its focused tests passed, but an unexplained loopback result and incomplete dependency/model tests mean the security proof is not accepted. The service remains disabled, with no timer.

sections.heading: The scheduled handoff needs diagnosis
sections.text: The November 11 scheduled handoff failed in the step that validates and publishes authorized packet pairs. An earlier run succeeded. The job summary identifies the failing stage but not the root cause, so this is a CI failure rather than proof that any packet was dispatched or altered.

insights.title: Isolation code is not isolation acceptance
insights.explanation: The tests support parts of the design, but the unresolved host anomalies prevent treating the proposed worker as a trusted execution boundary.

insights.title: Automatic handoff remains a separate operational gate
insights.explanation: The failed scheduled job is relevant even though the findings recovery pair was intentionally switched to manual handoff. A failed workflow does not establish whether other eligible pairs were affected.

article.takeaway: Worker isolation is an unmerged, incompletely accepted proof; scheduled packet-authoring handoff has a new failed run requiring diagnosis.
article.next_watch: Inspect the failed handoff step's bounded logs, then resolve the worker proof anomalies before independent review and any activation.

stories.headline: Findings recovery is placed on an owner-decision hold; automatic handoff switched off
stories.summary: After landing a read-only findings recovery, CUSTODIAN blocked the implementation packet pending an owner-controlled approval design. PR #139 also changed both implementation and paired-review authoring handoffs to manual. No recovery apply, accepted review or host cleanup is established.
stories.body: Main a16fb3ec merges PR #139, changing authoring handoff from auto to manual for the findings-closeout implementation and paired review. Earlier PR #138 marked the implementation blocked with an open user-owned decision: whether to establish a signing credential unavailable to the executing agent. The paired review remains labeled ready/auto for dispatch, but its dependency is blocked and its authoring handoff is manual. The landed recovery implementation retains a read-only plan and deliberately disabled apply. No independent acceptance, execution, or canonical teardown is established. GitHub-only partial coverage; no fresh private observation counts.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN has tightened the brakes on its findings-closeout repair. The recovery code has landed, but the task is now explicitly blocked on a decision only the project owner can make. sections.heading: A safeguard becomes an explicit project gate
